category_title: Disruptive student-teacher who publicly challenges instructor authority
student_description: Shelli is a middle-aged ultra-orthodox student who publicly challenges instructor authority and disrupts class when course content conflicts with her religious worldview. She frequently speaks out of turn, publishes public complaints, and demands personal attention to argue her points. The evidence reveals she uniquely requires strict, concise boundary-setting, professional distance (no extra 1-on-1 time), and appeals to her own religious or educational frameworks to manage her rebellion.

criteria.rationale: Shelli's public manifestos and abrupt departures are designed to disrupt; maintaining the routine proves her tactics will not alter the course.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan explicitly commits to continuing the standard teaching routine and syllabus without altering demands or showing emotional disruption from her outbursts.

criteria.rationale: Shelli needs to realize she is subject to the exact same expectations as everyone else, requiring continuous, neutral repetition of standard rules.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term strategy includes repeatedly enforcing standard classroom rules (e.g., raising hands, punctuality) for Shelli exactly as they do for the rest of the class.
